title: Regional public transport workers hold two-day strike in the Netherlands

tea.why: Negotiations for a new collective bargaining agreement for regional public transport workers collapsed last month.
tea.want: A new collective bargaining agreement for regional transport workers.
tea.changed: Nov 24: The second day of the strike concluded with continued disruptions to regional bus and train services across the Netherlands.

summary: Regional public transport workers in the Netherlands participated in a two-day strike on November 23 and 24, 2026, following the breakdown of collective bargaining agreement negotiations. Organised by the trade unions FNV and CNV, the action caused significant disruptions to regional bus, tram, and train services. According to union officials, approximately 80 percent of regional buses remained out of service on the first day. While the strike affected various regions, services operated by NS and city-specific transporters in Amsterdam, Rotterdam, and The Hague were not included as they operate under separate agreements. Unions have indicated that further industrial action is scheduled for December if their demands remain unmet. Transport companies reported varying levels of service impact depending on the region and worker participation.
response: No official response reported in the sources.

updates.text: Trade unions announce a two-day strike for regional public transport workers.
The first day of the strike takes place, with unions reporting that 80 percent of regional buses did not operate.
The second day of the strike causes continued service disruptions across various regions.
